title: Rectangle correction makes bounded component primitives pointwise finite
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended nonarchimedean norm [def-weil-algebraic-closure], [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], a profinite space $S$ (compact Hausdorff with clopen basis), a profinite group $G$ (compact Hausdorff with open normal subgroup basis), and $n\geq1$. All spaces use [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $C^r(P,G;V)=C(P\times G^r,V)$ for all continuous maps, with trivial group action, $d^0=0$, and for $r\geq1$
$$(dc)(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{r+1})=c(s;g_2,\ldots,g_{r+1})+\sum_{a=1}^r(-1)^a c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_ag_{a+1},\ldots,g_{r+1})+(-1)^{r+1}c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_r).$$
Let $F_i\subseteq\Omega$ be increasing intermediate fields finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $p_i:\Omega\to F_i$ linear over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, continuous, fixing $F_i$, with norm at most one; set $p_{-1}=0$. Let $z\in C^n(S,G;\Omega)$ be a cocycle and $e_i=(p_i-p_{i-1})z$. Assume $\|e_i\|_\infty\to0$ and that each fixed evaluation of $e_i$ is eventually zero.
Suppose, for $j\geq1$, rectangles $B_j=H_ja_{j,0}\times\cdots\times H_ja_{j,n}$, with $H_j$ open normal subgroups of $G$, and integers $N_j\geq0$ are given. Suppose locally constant finite-range $k_i:S\to\mathbf N_{\geq1}$ eventually stabilize at each $s$ to an index $j(s)$ for which the homogeneous function $f_z(s;g_0,\ldots,g_n)=z(s;g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1}^{-1}g_n)$ takes values in $F_{N_{j(s)}}$ on $B_{j(s)}$.
For each $j$, suppose coefficient-independent operators $T_j:C^n(*,G;V)\to C^{n-1}(*,G;V)$ and $R_j:C^n(*,G;V)\to C^n(*,G;V)$ are given for $V=F_i,\Omega$, by fixed finite sums of continuous evaluations with coefficients in $\mathbf Q_\ell$ of norm at most one. Assume they have norm at most one, preserve coefficient subspaces and continuous parameter families, and for every cocycle $c$ satisfy $dT_jc+R_jc=c$, $dR_jc=0$, and $R_jc=0$ whenever $f_c$ vanishes on $B_j$. Suppose $F_i$-linear contractions $h_i:C^n(*,G;F_i)\to C^{n-1}(*,G;F_i)$ send continuous profinite families to continuous families and satisfy $\|h_i c\|_\infty\leq\|c\|_\infty$ for all $c$ and $dh_ic=c$ on cocycles.
Then the fibrewise formulas
$$r_i(s)=R_{k_i(s)}e_i(s),\qquad b_i(s)=T_{k_i(s)}e_i(s)+h_i(r_i(s))$$
define continuous $F_i$-valued cochains with $db_i=e_i$ and $\|b_i\|_\infty\leq\|e_i\|_\infty\to0$. For every fixed $(s,x)\in S\times G^{n-1}$, $b_i(s,x)=0$ for all sufficiently large $i$. More precisely, eventually $R_{j(s)}e_i(s)=0$ as an entire cochain, and $b_i(s,x)=(T_{j(s)}e_i(s))(x)$ is a fixed finite sum of evaluations of $e_i$. Empty $S$ is allowed.

proof.text: For $i\geq1$, the inclusion $F_{i-1}\subseteq F_i$ makes $e_i=(p_i-p_{i-1})z$ a continuous $F_i$-valued cochain; for $i=0$ this is $p_0z$. All field topologies are the restricted norm topology. The displayed differential is a finite sum of evaluations with signs, so $d(p_i z)=p_i(dz)=0$ by $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linearity (also for $p_{-1}=0$). Hence $de_i=0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3) supplies motivation only; agent proof of the analytic auxiliary lemma, using its explicitly assumed operators and contractions.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and $j$. The hypotheses on $R_j,T_j$ and $h_i$ applied to the continuous family $e_i$ give continuous $F_i$-valued families $R_j e_i$, $T_j e_i$ and $T_j e_i+h_i(R_j e_i)$ on their respective products with $S$. At any $s$, local constancy of $k_i$ provides an open neighborhood on which $k_i=j=k_i(s)$. On that neighborhood the proposed $r_i,b_i$ equal these fixed-$j$ families. Continuity is local, so the formulas give continuous $F_i$-valued cochains on all of $S$.

source.place: Paragraph (3) supplies motivation only; agent proof of the analytic auxiliary lemma, using its explicitly assumed operators and contractions.

proof.text: For fixed $s$ put $j=k_i(s)$ and $c=e_i(s,-)$. This is a cocycle by step 1. The assumed identities give $dR_jc=0$ and $dh_i(R_jc)=R_jc$. Consequently $db_i(s,-)=dT_jc+dh_i(R_jc)=(c-R_jc)+R_jc=c$. Since $d$ never changes the parameter $s$, this proves $db_i=e_i$.

source.place: Paragraph (3) supplies motivation only; agent proof of the analytic auxiliary lemma, using its explicitly assumed operators and contractions.

proof.text: Put $E_i=\|e_i\|_\infty$. For each $s$ and $j=k_i(s)$, the assumed norm bounds give $\|T_j e_i(s,-)\|_\infty\leq E_i$, $\|R_j e_i(s,-)\|_\infty\leq E_i$, and $\|h_i(R_j e_i(s,-))\|_\infty\leq E_i$. At every evaluation the nonarchimedean inequality bounds the norm of their sum by $E_i$. Taking the supremum yields $\|b_i\|_\infty\leq E_i$. Thus $\|b_i\|_\infty\to0$ by the assumed convergence of $E_i$.

source.place: Paragraph (3) supplies motivation only; agent proof of the analytic auxiliary lemma, using its explicitly assumed operators and contractions.

proof.text: Fix $s$ and put $j=j(s)$ and $N=N_j$. Choose $I_s$ so that $k_i(s)=j$ for $i\geq I_s$. If also $i\geq N+1$, every value $v=f_z(s;g_0,\ldots,g_n)$ on $B_j$ lies in $F_N\subseteq F_{i-1}\subseteq F_i$, so $p_i(v)=p_{i-1}(v)=v$. Applying the homogeneous coordinate formula gives $f_{e_i(s,-)}=(p_i-p_{i-1})f_z(s,-)=0$ on the whole rectangle. The residual-vanishing assumption gives $R_j e_i(s,-)=0$ as an entire cochain. Coefficient independence identifies this equality for the $F_i$-valued and $\Omega$-valued formulas. Since $h_i$ is linear, $h_i(0)=0$, and therefore $b_i(s,x)=(T_j e_i(s,-))(x)$ for these $i$.

source.place: Paragraph (3) supplies motivation only; agent proof of the analytic auxiliary lemma, using its explicitly assumed operators and contractions.

proof.text: Now fix also $x\in G^{n-1}$. Write the stipulated fixed finite evaluation formula as $(T_j c)(x)=\sum_{a=1}^{u_j}\lambda_{j,a}c(\psi_{j,a}(x))$. For every one of the finitely many points $(s,\psi_{j,a}(x))$, choose a threshold beyond which $e_i$ is zero there, using the pointwise hypothesis. The maximum of these thresholds, $I_s$ and $N_j+1$ works simultaneously. Step 5 then makes $b_i(s,x)$ a sum of zeros. An empty evaluation list already gives zero. When $n=1$, $G^0$ is a singleton and the same calculation uses the stipulated $d^0=0$. When $S$ is empty all cochains are the unique empty functions, their supremum norms are zero, and all assertions hold.
